behavior: A settlement's transaction hash is recorded only when our own settle transaction succeeded
acceptance: When a sent settlement intent finds the receiver already settled (for example the refund authority settled after the deadline), the signer checks our transaction's receipt and keeps its tx_hash only if it succeeded, otherwise stores no hash; settlementTxHash and activity txHash are then null as openapi.yaml and api.md already say; a signer test on Anvil covers a sent intent that the refund authority settles
notes: 2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: Pass. confirmIfFinal (all 3 confirm paths) keeps tx_hash only on a status-1 receipt; settle() reverts AlreadySettled, so status 1 proves ours settled; receiver-settled is read at finalized, so a later reorg can't change the settler. Booking/idempotency unchanged (FOR UPDATE status check). Non-NotFound RPC errors are wrapped and retried next round, consistent with reconcile. Known limit: single primary RPC; a lagging/pruned node returning NotFound for our mined settle stores a null hash (display-only, money unaffected). Backend tests pass; disabling the receipt check makes both new subtests fail.

proof.1: backend: internal/settlement TestSettledByTheRefundAuthorityAfterOurSettleFailedHasNoTxHash (Anvil + Postgres; subtests reverted, never mined): our settle is saved, then after the deadline it reverts (receipt status 0) or is never sent, and the refund authority settles the receiver; the signer confirms the intent, the invoice is settled, the recipient gets 5000000, the settlement is booked once in ledger_transactions, and GET-invoice settlementTxHash (invoice.Service.Get, same tx_hash column activity reads) is null. TestSettlesAPaidInvoiceOnce now also asserts the normal path's settlementTxHash is our settle with a successful receipt. Both subtests failed before the fix (the failed hash was recorded).
